ideas.title: A marble that bends light (a toy, not gravity)
ideas.critique: This is round 1's pebble of bent light without the pull. That removes the part that repeated the ring's gravity rule and keeps the part no engine does: rays bent inside the tracer. The peekaboo will probably play as a scripted reaction, so the surprise comes from the ring itself. A screen-space warp in raster and the browser is a cheap fake that weakens it everywhere except the traced film.

ideas.title: The camera obscura hut
ideas.critique: A picture of the live island shown inside the island is the payoff the TV already gave, and a hut is one more place. Forming the image through a lens by light transport alone is a caustic path that a plain path tracer renders as noise. Unless that is solved, the honest version is the raster fallback, and that makes this a projector.

ideas.title: They stole the camera
ideas.critique: The viewpoint having its own life has been done once with the bored camera. Here the friends act on the camera, and a refracting smear on the lens is a real material trick. Being carried off at crab height and wriggling free is something a player would do again. The risk is that grab and pass is one scripted chase, and a shaky carried view is unpleasant to watch.

ideas.title: Dance with your late reflection
ideas.critique: This is round 1's slow mirror pond with a canon and a lead the player controls. It is still a time-shifted copy of the island, like the TV. Making it playable, so that the player's own move comes back twice and fainter, is the real step. The group canon will read as choreography unless the friends really pick moves off each other.

ideas.title: The player's hand
ideas.critique: A floating hand that picks up and pokes is a known god-game device, so the shape is expected. Direct touch with a reaction from every creature is the thing the island most lacks for play, and it is what someone shows a friend. It stands or falls on the reactions feeling physical (toppling, dangling, complaining) rather than a canned animation per click.

ideas.title: Dreams in the night sky
ideas.critique: Pictures hung in the sky above friends lying below is close to the cloud-shape events, and generated images on flat sheets will look like billboards. Emissive sheets that really light the night island in the tracer, and that come from the creatures' real memories, are new. There is little to come back to after one night.

ideas.title: Snowballs that grow as they roll
ideas.critique: A ground layer that piles up and gets reshaped is the recipe the sand dunes used, and rolling, stacking and flattening things are what the physics goal asks for. Balls that really grow with the snow they take and leave a carved green trail are a satisfying toy the player would push again. The look-alike snowman is the scripted part.

ideas.title: Cut the island open
ideas.critique: Splitting the island apart is a whole-island wreck in the line of the seesaw and the turtle. The interior is a set of generated props seen once, and then the halves close. A clipping-plane section with a glowing crystal vein is a nice traced shot, but nothing in it moves, plays or stays.
